title: short-rate-anomaly-regimes: replication and monetary-regime extension of short-rate asset-pricing anomaly models
description:
Research compendium for the paper Short Term Interest Rate Innovations Across Monetary Regimes. The repository reconstructs and extends the two-factor ICAPM of Maio and Santa-Clara (2017, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 52(3), 927-961, DOI 10.1017/S002210901700028X), in which the pricing factors are the market excess return and the innovation in a short-term interest rate.

The empirical programme is complete. The compendium provides: immutable acquisition of public inputs with raw and normalized checksums, retrieval timestamps, vintage labels, and redistribution status; a verified audit of the monthly aggregation of the federal funds and three-month Treasury-bill rate series against their daily counterparts; AR(1) short-rate innovation reconstruction with an automatically tested pre-window timing convention; publication-era and current vintages of the Kenneth French, Hou-Xue-Zhang q-factor, and Pastor-Stambaugh liquidity files with a revision comparison; a validated canonical monthly panel for 1972-01 to 2013-12 and a vintage-consistent 648-month panel to 2025-12; the article's two-pass estimator with the Shanken correction applied to risk prices and pricing errors, estimated for eight models on eight asset sets; a cell-level audit against the published tables; weak-factor identification, influence and precision diagnostics; a post-publication extension that separates the data-vintage contribution from the temporal one; monetary-regime equivalence tests under a pre-registered two one-sided-tests rule with a joint moving-block bootstrap; pooled regime-interaction and structural-break batteries; and a simulation of what the two-pass estimator supports at regime-length samples.

Every threshold, comparator and decision rule was fixed before the corresponding estimate existed, and every registered gate is reported whether it passed or failed. The registered outcomes are that the baseline pattern reconstructs qualitatively while incremental pricing materiality (H1), post-publication compatibility (H2) and regime stability (H3) are unsupported against their predeclared standards, and the weak-factor conditions (H4a, H4b, H4c) pass. Result tables and figures in the manuscript are generated from the frozen artifacts rather than transcribed, and a drift guard fails if a committed table stops matching its source.

The design separates exact replication from documented reconstruction and never labels a reconstruction as replication. No input qualifies as exact, because the article names data providers and people rather than files; every derived analysis therefore carries a documented-reconstruction label, and the compendium supports statements about patterns rather than about the article's arithmetic. Per-layer classifications and the remaining blocking inputs are recorded in docs/REPLICATION_STATUS.md.

No raw data, licensed database extracts, or restricted author-provided files are redistributed, so the generated panels and estimate stores are not shipped. The archive carries the acquisition and estimation code, the frozen source registry, checksums and provenance manifests, and a deterministic make reproduce path that regenerates every empirical artifact from the frozen public sources. The release gate reports that distinction directly, evaluating file presence against the archive a recipient receives rather than against a working tree.

Public data sources used and separately licensed by their providers: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) at the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; the Kenneth R. French Data Library; the Hou, Xue, and Zhang q-factor library at global-q.org; and the Pastor-Stambaugh liquidity series published by Robert F. Stambaugh. Publication-era vintages were retrieved from the Internet Archive. This repository redistributes none of those files; it distributes the acquisition code, checksums, and provenance manifests needed to obtain and verify them.
